title: Doing it yourself or getting help

sections.skill: Compare the cost of help with the value of your own time and risk

questions.prompt: Earning 50 dollars an hour, an owner can pay a 35-dollar bookkeeper. What is the difference per hour?
questions.correct_answer: 15 dollars
questions.intro: Owners often try to do everything themselves to save money. Compare the cost of HIRING HELP with the value of your own time and the risk of mistakes. Example: if you can earn 50 dollars an hour on paid work and a bookkeeper charges 35 dollars an hour, paying the bookkeeper may free time for better-paid work. Get help for tasks that are complex, risky, or that you do slowly; keep tasks that are simple and central to your business. Start small, for example a few hours a month.

questions.prompt: You earn 60 dollars an hour; help costs 30. What is the net gain per freed hour?
questions.correct_answer: 30 dollars
questions.intro: To compare doing a task yourself with paying someone, look at the value per hour. If you can earn 40 dollars an hour on paid work and a helper charges 25 dollars an hour, each hour you hand off can free you to earn 40 instead. The net gain per hour is 40 - 25 = 15 dollars, if you really fill the freed hour with paid work. If you cannot, the gain is smaller.
